author: agent
text:
Re-read after 0.54.0. The parse-cache comment correction recorded in the confirm below still holds - it names PARSE_SCHEMA_VERSION rather than citing line numbers, which is why it survived this release unscathed while the line numbers it used to cite have moved again.

New here, and the reason the older confirms went stale: __init__ now sets self.stale_sketches = False, and load_existing() reads the stored sketch generation BEFORE anything overwrites it, setting that flag when the sketches on disk came from a different shingle hash than this build's. cmd_index reads the flag and passes use_sketch=not migrating to detect_lineage, which is what keeps a migrating index from asserting deletions it cannot know.

Order matters in load_existing: the generation must be read before the coordinates are loaded and before anything re-stamps the manifest. Moving that read later would make every map look current, which is the precise failure the flag exists to prevent.

_recover_from_snapshot() is unchanged and still restores identities (and therefore attached knowledge) from versions/ after a corrupted index - note that versions/ is gitignored, so that recovery path exists only on the machine that built the snapshots, never in a fresh clone.

author: agent
text:
Re-read after 0.54.1. Everything the previous confirms recorded still holds - including the parse-cache comment naming PARSE_SCHEMA_VERSION instead of line numbers, which is why it has now survived two releases while the lines it used to cite moved twice.

New: index() takes a keyword-only persist flag, defaulting True. persist=False computes in memory and writes NOTHING - the parse-cache refresh at the end of index() is the only write this method makes on its own, and read surfaces that need current-tree hashes (verify_change) pair it with load_existing(write_cache=False) and never call save().

Keyword-only and defaulted for a reason: index() has 41 direct callers and complexity 26, so a positional flag here would eventually be passed by accident, and any default other than True would silently change behaviour for all of them.

Unchanged from 0.54.0 and still load-bearing: self.stale_sketches, set in load_existing by reading the stored sketch generation BEFORE anything overwrites it. Order matters - move that read later and every map looks current, which is the exact failure the flag exists to prevent.

A standing rule for this class, worth repeating because it is the one that cost a year: anything persisted into coordinates.json must be reproducible by a different process on a different machine. builtin hash(), id(), and set/dict iteration order leaking into a written list are all disqualified. tests/test_determinism.py holds the line and deliberately does not pin PYTHONHASHSEED.

author: cli
text: Re-read after 0.54.3. Everything the confirms below record still holds - the parse-cache comment naming PARSE_SCHEMA_VERSION rather than line numbers, stale_sketches read before anything overwrites it, and index(persist=False) writing nothing. New here: load_raw_edges IGNORES fields this build does not know, filtering the JSON row against RawEdge's declared fields before construction. Measured the hard way - 0.54.3 added RawEdge.via_attr, and a long-running MCP server started before the upgrade crashed on 'unexpected keyword argument' the moment the map was re-indexed by the new build. Unknown keys are dropped rather than refused: an older build then behaves exactly as it did before the field existed, which is the honest degradation. It cannot use information it has no code for, and refusing to start is a worse answer than working without it. Same principle as an absent sketch stamp reading as generation 1.
